q-222766.name: Question 1
q-222766.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14155061/assets/d9884bf61d9b904b3e6846e6a1d307e34e1b84023e8e5a321c09be6bfd44069c.png)

Use the model above to compute the following result. Express your answer as a fraction in its lowest terms.

$\frac{1}{5}÷\frac{3}{5}=$
{{field-1}}
q-222766.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14155061/assets/327c59257b6ea1d0b18f73bcff065a8ddade49db9ce6b84ba44c824d1c041901.png)

We can break down our division problem as follows:

- Computing $\frac{1}{5}÷\frac{3}{5}$ means we want to determine how many times $\frac{3}{5}$ fits into $\frac{1}{5}.$

- Since both fractions have a *common denominator*, this is the *same* as determining how many times $3$ fits into $1.$

- Therefore, instead of $\frac{1}{5}÷\frac{3}{5}$, we can simply compute $1÷3.$

So, we have

$$
1÷3=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{1}{5}÷\frac{3}{5}=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Use the model above to compute the following result. Express your answer as a fraction in its lowest terms.

{{field-1}}
q-222987.worked_solution:
The denominators are $4$ and $7.$ We can make a common denominator of $4\times 7=28.$ 

We split the shape on the left of the division sign into $7$ parts vertically, and we split the shape on the right into $4$ parts horizontally:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14155061/assets/919b2e3f87aabf375cb968e876ee19b0ce9cd6a70c41088b062459a1f4f1f133.png)

So, our division problem now is

$$
\frac{21}{28}÷\frac{24}{28}.
$$

Since the denominators are equal, this is equivalent to

$$
21÷24=\frac{21}{24}=\frac{7}{8}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{3}{4}÷\frac{6}{7}=\frac{7}{8}.
$$

q-61482.worked_solution:
The denominators are $4$ and $6.$ We can make a common denominator of $12.$ 

We split the shape on the left of the division sign into $3$ parts vertically, and we split the shape on the right into $4$ parts horizontally:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14155061/assets/2b342d9977254cd8af8fb93fe632f4c154b6f797e3fcb89bdfc91945f7736dd1.png)

So, our division problem now is

$$
\frac{9}{12}÷\frac{6}{12}.
$$

Since the denominators are equal, this is equivalent to

$$
9÷6=1\,\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{3}{4}÷\frac{3}{6}=1\,\frac{1}{2}.
$$

q-61395.name: Question 8
q-61395.worked_solution:
The denominators are $3$ and $4.$ We can make a common denominator of $12.$ 

We split the shape on the left of the division sign into $3$ parts vertically, and we split the shape on the right into $4$ parts horizontally:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14155061/assets/1e7a163bb4ee9efb6574e55a37ddeeac3503f2b2b873ba7ba253a969c92d3bb7.png)

So, our division problem now is

$$
\frac{9}{12}÷\frac{8}{12}.
$$

Since the denominators are equal, this is equivalent to

$$
9÷8=1\,\frac{1}{8}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{3}{4}÷\frac{2}{3}=1\,\frac{1}{8}.
$$

q-61604.name: Question 9
q-61604.worked_solution:
The denominators are $5$ and $10.$ We can make a common denominator of $10.$

We split the shape on the right of the division sign into $2$ parts vertically:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14155061/assets/43424ef31fc44fa8485ee7a7b5a0ce6855858ad477d8365ac2ad898d25353f29.png)

$$
\frac{7}{10}÷\frac{6}{10}.

$$

$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{7}{10}÷\frac{3}{5}=1\,\frac{1}{6}.
$$
